newsitem.title: UK: UK's Labour set to scrap reform on mergers - paper.
newsitem.headline: UK's Labour set to scrap reform on mergers - paper.

text.p: Britain's opposition Labour Party is set to abandon its plan to reform competition policy amid concerns it might lose votes from the business community, said the Financial Times newspaper.
The proposal to make companies prove that planned takeovers are in the "public interest" is set to be dropped after a review ordered by Labour leader Tony Blair, said the article.

The review team, made up of Lord Borrie, former director general of the Office of Fair Trading, Bryan Sanderson, managing director of BP Chemicals and John Vickers, professor of political economy at Oxford University, is expected to deliver its verdict by the end of the month.
